notes: Lead with dairy as cash-flow smoothing, not as a side activity. Point to the left-right contrast: districts with stronger livestock income dependence are less tied to one crop cycle. Expect a question on whether this is productivity or participation; answer that this slide proves income broadening first.
title: Livestock and dairy broaden Gujarat’s rural income base by reducing dependence on a single crop season
subtitle: Milk income arrives throughout the year, so districts with stronger livestock participation have a second earnings rail alongside commercial crops; that diversification matters most where crop income is exposed to rainfall, price swings, and seasonal harvest concentration.

chart.annotation: Livestock income is widespread in key districts, showing dairy is a material second income stream beyond crop harvests.
chart.source: Source: NSS, NDDB, state livestock assessments 2024-2025 [[src:official]]

insights.text: **Banaskantha** leads at **68%**[[src:official]], making it the clearest proof that livestock is not peripheral in Gujarat’s farm economy; a majority of households already draw earnings from an activity that pays across the year rather than at one harvest moment.

The pattern is broad across dairy-linked districts: **Ahmedabad** reaches **62%**[[src:official]], **Kheda** **57%**[[src:official]], **Junagadh** **53%**[[src:official]], and **Rajkot** **49%**[[src:official]], showing that livestock income complements commercial cropping across multiple production geographies.

**Surendranagar** at **28%**[[src:official]] marks the lower end of participation, which sharpens the intervention case: where livestock is less embedded, households remain more exposed to a single crop season and have less built-in earnings diversification.

footnote: Livestock-income participation by district is shown as evidence that dairy broadens rural earnings beyond crop-season cash flow. Source: NSS, NDDB, state livestock assessments 2024-2025 [[src:official]]
